Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: REFRAME
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: None of the three options can be delivered. Option A needs the pipeline to close this issue and file a new one, and the pipeline only changes files and opens one pull request. Option B ships tests that fail, which the issue's own rules forbid. Option C cannot work: implement enforces the frozen `ai:workflow-heal-scope:v1` marker whatever the approval (agents.md line 1997, `scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh`, `scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:351-353` → `out_of_heal_scope`). A fix inside the allowed scope does exist. `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` (allowed) can print the failure reason on a runtime line that the current `_SOFT_LOG_PATTERNS` (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:601-605`) already keeps. The fix to the filter itself in `workflow_failure_heal.py` goes under deferred scope instead of being forced through this heal.
Q2: The crash cause is not in the repository, and option B needs someone to paste log lines that nobody can supply here (data-provision guard). Option A is the conservative choice. Once this change lands, the next clarify failure's heal report will contain the `CLAUDE_POOL run … outcome= reason=` data needed to fix the crash.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/clarify.yml` lines 1655-1695 ("Run Codex" retry loop). On a nonzero `rc` it prints only `::warning::${clarify_engine_name} exited with code $rc on attempt ${attempt}.` (line 1686). In the raw log the runner writes that as `##[warning]…`, which the filter drops: it matches `::warning::` but not `##[warning]`, and "exited with code" is not `\bexit code\b`.
    - `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh:322-325`. The Claude CLI stderr is copied to the third argument (`${RUNTIME_DIR}/codex_log.txt`) and to stderr. The `CLAUDE_POOL run role=… account=… outcome=… reason=… exit_code=…` line goes to stderr only (line 325), so clarify.yml can capture it from the call's stderr without changing the script.
    - `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` `_SOFT_LOG_PATTERNS` (lines 601-605). It keeps `\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_(?:FAILED|SKIPPED|ESCALATE|BLOCKED)\b`, `\bERROR\b` and `\bFAIL(?:ED|URE)?\b`. `filter_log` and `_drop_step_script_lines` are read and used by the tests only; this plan does not edit them.
    - Allowed paths: the heal-scope marker (`.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `tests/**`, `changelog.d/*.md`) plus this issue's own `agents.d/<N>-*.md` fragment (agents.md line 1997, #8064).
  steps:
    - In the clarify.yml retry loop, keep the existing `::warning::… exited with code …` line unchanged, since it is an existing log message. Add one plain stdout line per failed attempt, under a new prefix that ends in `_FAILED` (for example `CLARIFY_ENGINE_ATTEMPT_FAILED engine=<name> attempt=<n> exit_code=<rc> pool_outcome=<v> pool_reason=<v>`). Check the name does not collide with an existing prefix (grep agents.md and scripts/). The `pool_*` fields come from the last `CLAUDE_POOL run ` line that this attempt's `clarify_isolated_run.sh` call wrote to stderr. Capture that stderr into a runtime file and pass it on to the log unchanged. Only the whitelisted key=value tokens (`role`, `account`, `outcome`, `reason`, `exit_code`) are re-emitted. Each value is limited to `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` and to at most 64 characters, and is `unknown` when no line exists (Codex path, or a crash before line 325). Raw CLI stderr is never re-emitted. Do not use `::error::` per attempt, because retries that later succeed would leave error annotations.
    - Leave exit codes, retry counts, sleeps, the `rc` 75/76/80 handling and the final `::error::… clarify failed after … attempts.` line exactly as they are.
    - Add a regression test under `tests/` (for example `tests/test_clarify_attempt_failure_reason_log.py`) that:
      - (a) extracts the Run Codex step body from clarify.yml and asserts it emits the new `_FAILED` line built from the captured `CLAUDE_POOL run` fields;
      - (b) builds a synthetic raw job log shaped like run 41287557900: a `##[group]Run` header whose script lines lack the ANSI cyan prefix, then `##[endgroup]`, then the runtime lines `##[warning]Claude exited with code 1 on attempt 1.` and the new line with `pool_outcome=crashed pool_reason=no_result exit_code=1`. It feeds that log through the real `workflow_failure_heal.filter_log` and asserts the new line survives with `pool_reason=no_result`;
      - (c) runs the extracted loop with a stub `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` that writes `CLAUDE_POOL run role=CLARIFY account=TEAM1 outcome=crashed reason=no_result exit_code=1` to stderr and exits 1, with sleeps disabled, and asserts the emitted line has the expected fields. If extraction makes this too brittle, (a)+(b) are the minimum.
      Run the test against the pinned head (fails: no such line is emitted) and with the fix (passes), and record both runs in the PR.
    - Add `changelog.d/<N>-clarify-attempt-failure-reason.md`. Add `agents.d/<N>-clarify-attempt-failure-reason.md` with a `<!-- agents: section="Stable log prefixes (contractual)" -->` block registering the new prefix (bullet plus `LOG_PREFIX.name=` line).
    - Run `wc -c .github/workflows/clarify.yml` and confirm it stays under 480,000 bytes.
    - In the plan, write `## Deferred scope` with bullets for `clarify` (the Claude crash on btc_sweeper#248, cause unknown until the new line is visible) and for the `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` filter fix: add `##\[warning\]`, the `CLAUDE_POOL run … outcome=(?!success)` alternative and `AI_ENGINE_FALLBACK\w*` to `_SOFT_LOG_PATTERNS`, and fix the non-cyan `_drop_step_script_lines` case, both with tests in `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py`. The plan ends its `## Counterfactual check` with `HEAL_COUNTERFACTUAL: PARTIAL: clarify`, because the clarify job would still fail on the unknown crash. Add no steps that file or close issues.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: The suggested fix, extending `_SOFT_LOG_PATTERNS` and `_drop_step_script_lines` in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` and adding tests in `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py`.
  equivalence_argument: The concrete failure was that the heal evidence for a clarify crash did not contain the line naming its cause. After this change every failed clarify attempt prints that cause (pool outcome, reason, exit code) on a line that the shipped filter, unchanged, provably keeps. The test runs the real `filter_log`, so it fails on the reported head and passes with the fix, which satisfies the issue's rule that the regression test must fail before and pass after. The general filter weakness, which also affects other workflows, is not hidden: it is tracked in deferred scope, so the issue stays open after the merge.
  reversibility: The change is one extra log line and the capture of stderr into a runtime file; the exit status and retry behaviour stay the same. Reverting the clarify.yml hunk and deleting the test and fragments restores the current behaviour exactly. If a maintainer later fixes the filter in `workflow_failure_heal.py` through a normal issue, the extra line is redundant but harmless.
